title: Employment Agreement | Free Word Template
description: Free employment agreement template: hire a new employee with terms for pay, duties, benefits, IP and termination.
lead: A contract between an employer and employee setting out the terms of employment — role, compensation, benefits, work hours, intellectual property, confidentiality and how employment can end.
introParagraphs: An employment agreement (or employment contract) is signed when a new hire starts work. It sets out the key terms of the job — title, pay, hours, benefits, leave, confidentiality, IP assignment, non-compete/non-solicit and termination — so both sides know where they stand.

At-will employment is the default in most US states, but a written agreement is still useful for IP assignment, confidentiality, bonus/commission terms, and any restrictive covenants. Have an attorney review restrictive covenants as enforceability varies widely by state.
bullets: Parties and role
Employer name and address; employee name and address; job title; department; start date; reports-to; work location (and remote-work terms).
Compensation
Base salary or hourly rate, pay frequency, overtime eligibility, bonus/commission structure, equity if any, paydays.
Benefits and leave
Health insurance, retirement plan, PTO/sick leave, holidays, parental leave, and other benefits (and when eligibility starts).
Duties and expectations
Core responsibilities, work hours, at-will or fixed-term status, performance review schedule, and any probation period.
Legal clauses
Intellectual property assignment, confidentiality, non-compete/non-solicit (as enforceable), return of property, dispute resolution (arbitration/mediation), and termination terms.
howTo: Finalise the offer first
Agree on salary, title, start date and key terms verbally or in an offer letter before drafting the agreement.
Use compliant language
Make sure restrictive covenants meet your state rules (non-competes are banned or unenforceable for many workers post-2024).
Spell out compensation clearly
State base pay, bonus formula (discretionary vs formulaic), commission triggers and paydays explicitly.
Include IP and confidentiality
Assign work product to the company and require confidentiality of company information; include a return-of-property clause.
Sign before day one
Both parties sign before or on the start date; employee gets a fully signed copy. File with HR records.
related: Shorter offer letter that often precedes the employment agreement.
Confidentiality standalone if not inside the employment agreement.
Proof-of-employment letter for lenders and landlords.
faq: Is an employment agreement required?
No in the US (at-will is the default) but strongly recommended for IP assignment, confidentiality and clear terms.
Can I change it after signing?
Only with the employee written consent; material changes without consent can be unenforceable.
Are non-competes enforceable?
They are banned for most workers under the 2024 FTC rule (currently under litigation) and heavily restricted in many states; consult counsel.
Do I need one for every employee?
It is best practice for exempt/professional roles and any role with IP access; offer letters can suffice for hourly staff if you cover IP/confidentiality.
At-will vs fixed-term?
At-will means either side can end it any time for a lawful reason; fixed-term sets an end date and usually requires cause or notice to terminate early.

title: Employment Termination Letter | Free Word Template
description: Free employment termination letter: formal notice of job termination with final pay, benefits and return of property.
lead: A formal letter notifying an employee their employment has ended (with or without cause), stating the last day, final pay, benefits continuation (COBRA) and next steps for returning company property.
introParagraphs: An employment termination letter (or separation letter) formally ends employment. It states the reason (if given), last day worked, final pay details, what happens to benefits/accrued PTO, COBRA notice, and how to return company property.

Keep the letter factual and concise. For involuntary terminations, deliver in person (or by email/certified post if remote) and have a witness present. Follow your state final-pay rules or you may face waiting-time penalties.
bullets: Employee and role
Employee name, job title, department, manager, and termination effective date (and last day worked if different).
Reason (optional)
Brief reason for termination: redundancy, performance, misconduct, mutual separation, or end of fixed term. Avoid editorialising.
Final pay
Final pay amount, pay date, accrued but unused PTO payout (as required by state law), deductions, and how it will be delivered.
Benefits and severance
What happens to health insurance (COBRA), retirement, equity vesting/exercise window, and any severance pay (typically conditional on a separation/release agreement).
Property return and next steps
List company property to return (laptop, phone, keys, badge, ID), return deadline, and contact for questions (HR).
howTo: Prepare in advance
Coordinate with HR/legal; confirm final-pay calculation under state law and any severance package.
Hold the termination meeting
Deliver the news in a short meeting (10-15 minutes) with a witness present; hand over the letter.
Be clear and respectful
State the decision directly, explain final pay/benefits briefly, and avoid debate.
Collect company property
Arrange for laptop, keys, badge and access cards to be returned immediately or within a set deadline; revoke system access.
Send follow-up paperwork
Email the letter, COBRA notice and separation agreement (if any) to the employee; keep a signed copy.
related: Offered in exchange for a release of claims.
Progressive-discipline step that usually precedes for-cause termination.
faq: Do I have to give a reason?
In at-will states generally no, but stating a brief factual reason reduces wrongful-termination claims. You must give a reason for discriminatory/retaliatory-protected positions.
When must final pay be issued?
Immediately in some states (e.g. California), within 72 hours or next payday in others — check your state.
Can I email the letter?
Yes, especially for remote workers; hand delivery is more respectful for in-person employees.
Do I have to offer severance?
No unless a contract or policy promises it; severance is usually exchanged for a signed release of claims.
What about unused PTO?
Many states require paying out accrued, unused PTO; some do not. Check local rules.

title: Severance Agreement | Free Word Template
description: Free severance agreement: offer severance pay and benefits in exchange for a release of claims.
lead: A contract between employer and departing employee offering a severance package (pay, continued benefits, outplacement) in exchange for a release of legal claims against the company.
introParagraphs: A severance agreement (or separation agreement) offers a departing employee extra compensation or benefits beyond what they are owed, in exchange for signing a general release of claims against the employer. It may also include non-disparagement, confidentiality and cooperation clauses.

Workers over 40 have special protections under the OWBPA (part of the Age Discrimination in Employment Act): they must be given at least 21 (or 45 in a group layoff) days to consider the agreement and 7 days to revoke after signing. Have counsel review agreements involving laid-off employees or workers over 40.
bullets: Parties and date
Employer and employee names, date of agreement, last day of employment.
Severance payments
Amount of severance pay (often X weeks per year of service), pay schedule (lump sum or salary continuation), and when payments begin.
Benefits continuation
Continued health-insurance premiums, outplacement services, equity treatment (extended exercise window), and accrued bonus/commission owed.
Release of claims
Employee releases known and unknown claims against the company (and affiliates, officers, employees) up to the signing date, excluding non-waivable claims.
Other clauses
Non-disparagement (mutual where allowed), confidentiality of the agreement terms, return of company property, cooperation in future matters, non-compete/non-solicit confirmation, and governing law.
howTo: Decide the package
Set severance amount, benefit continuation and any extras based on tenure, role and the circumstances.
Comply with OWBPA if over 40
Include the 21/45-day consideration period, 7-day revocation period and (for group layoffs) the required disclosure of job titles/ages.
Attach the release
List categories of claims released and explicitly carve out non-waivable rights (workers comp, unemployment, vested benefits, right to report to agencies).
Present after termination
Hand or send the agreement after the termination meeting; give the employee the legally required time to review and sign.
Pay on schedule
Make the first severance payment once any revocation period has expired; continue per the schedule.
related: Notice letter delivered alongside or before the severance offer.
Progressive discipline that usually precedes termination.
For ongoing confidentiality beyond the agreement.
faq: Is severance required?
No unless an employment contract, policy, or plan promises it. Most severance is voluntary in exchange for a release.
Can an employee sue after signing?
Only for claims that cannot be waived by law (e.g. workers comp, certain wage claims, future discrimination, right to file with EEOC).
What is the OWBPA?
The Older Workers Benefit Protection Act: requires 21 days (45 in group layoffs) to review and 7 days to revoke for workers over 40.
Do I need to pay extra for non-disparagement?
In some states (e.g. California), non-disparagement/confidentiality clauses in severance require an additional payment and cannot prevent disclosure of unlawful acts.
How much severance is typical?
1-2 weeks of pay per year of service is common for individual contributors; more for executives. There is no legal minimum.

title: Internship Offer Letter | Free Word Template
description: Free internship offer letter template: offer an intern role with pay, dates, hours, mentorship and academic credit terms.
lead: A letter offering an internship position (paid or unpaid) that states the role, start/end dates, hours, compensation/stipend, mentorship, supervisor, and whether academic credit is available.
introParagraphs: An internship offer letter formally offers a student or recent graduate an internship at your company. It sets out role expectations, duration, hours, compensation (paid, unpaid or stipend), mentorship plan and, where applicable, how academic credit works.

Unpaid internships at for-profit employers must satisfy strict criteria under the US Department of Labor primary-beneficiary test. If an intern is performing productive work that would otherwise be done by paid staff, they generally must be paid minimum wage.
bullets: Intern and role
Intern name, position/title, department, start date, end date, expected hours per week and on-site/remote location.
Compensation
Hourly pay (if paid), stipend amount and timing, expense reimbursement, and whether overtime is allowed.
Supervision and mentoring
Direct supervisor, the mentor assigned, check-in cadence and learning objectives.
Academic credit (if applicable)
Whether the internship qualifies for academic credit, documentation the intern must provide, and any school requirements for hours or deliverables.
At-will and compliance
Statement that the internship is not a guarantee of future employment, confidentiality/IP expectations, and company policies the intern must follow.
howTo: Decide paid vs unpaid
Apply the DOL primary-beneficiary test; err on the side of paid unless it is a structured educational program for credit.
Define learning objectives
Write 2-3 clear learning goals and name a mentor; this is required for unpaid/for-credit internships.
Set the dates and hours
Confirm the term length, weekly hours and whether the intern is expected around exam periods.
Confirm credit paperwork
If for school credit, coordinate with the university to understand required forms and mid-term/end-of-term evaluations.
Sign and welcome
Both parties sign; send welcome email with onboarding details, first-day logistics and who to report to.
related: For hiring a regular employee post-internship.
Detailed role duties often attached to the offer.
Confidentiality obligations for interns with access to company information.
faq: Can interns be unpaid?
Only if the intern is the primary beneficiary of the arrangement under DOL rules; for-profit companies must pay most interns for productive work.
Do interns need an agreement?
An offer letter is enough for short internships; add an NDA/IP agreement if they access confidential information or create work product.
Do interns get benefits?
Typically no — interns are usually not eligible for health/retirement benefits; paid interns are covered by workers comp.
Can I hire an intern full-time after?
Yes — internship-to-hire is common, but do not imply a job offer in the letter unless you intend to make one.
International students?
Students on F-1/J-1 visas often need CPT/OPT authorisation from their school before they can intern; coordinate with their DSO.

title: Contract Termination Letter | Free Word Template
description: Free contract termination letter: formally end a business contract with notice, effective date and transition terms.
lead: A formal letter notifying another party that you are terminating an existing contract — for cause, for convenience, or at the end of the term — and stating the effective date and transition obligations.
introParagraphs: A contract termination letter formally ends a business agreement. It identifies the contract, states why and when it ends (citing the relevant clause), and explains any wind-down obligations — final payments, return of materials, confidentiality survival, and transition assistance.

Check the contract termination clause carefully before sending: it usually dictates required notice period, method of delivery, cure periods for cause, and any early-termination fees. Deliver as required in the contract (certified mail, email to a specific address, etc.) and keep proof.
bullets: Parties and contract
Your name/company, the other party name/address, contract title and date, and any contract/PO number.
Reason for termination
Termination for cause (breach, non-payment, non-performance) with citation of the breached clause; or termination for convenience; or end of term/non-renewal.
Effective date
Date termination takes effect, calculated from proper notice per the contract.
Final obligations
Final invoices/payments owed, work-in-progress handoff, return of property/confidential information, and any wind-down assistance you will provide.
Surviving clauses
Confidentiality, IP ownership, liability, governing law and dispute-resolution clauses that survive termination.
howTo: Review the contract
Identify the termination clause, required notice period and delivery method; confirm any cure period before termination for cause.
Cite the reason clearly
Reference the breached section, prior cure notices sent, and why termination is triggered; for convenience just cite the clause.
Calculate the effective date
Set the date that satisfies the contractual notice period from proper service.
Spell out wind-down
List exactly what must be returned, paid or delivered, and by when; state what happens to in-progress work.
Deliver per the contract
Send by the method the contract requires (often certified mail + email); keep proof of service and a signed copy.
related: For ending a lease by mutual agreement.
Demand to stop harmful conduct before or alongside termination.
faq: Can I terminate any contract early?
Only if the contract allows it (for cause, for convenience) or the other party materially breaches; wrongfully terminating can be a breach itself.
What notice period is required?
Whatever the contract says — 30, 60 or 90 days is common; if silent, reasonable notice is implied.
Do I need a reason?
For convenience or end-of-term, no. For cause, cite the breach and give cure time if required.
Email enough?
Only if the contract allows email notice; many require certified mail or physical delivery to a specific address.
What about early-termination fees?
If the contract sets a fee, it is usually owed; challenge only if it is an unenforceable penalty.
